---
title: Enum
description: "One label from an application-declared list, such as a currency code."
---

`Enum` represents one label from an application-declared list. Suppose a
payment dataset records amounts in USD, EUR, or GBP. The example below adds
that currency code as context for predicting a later dispute. Keep currency
conversion and units in data preparation.

```python
import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.xs(
    amount=rf.Number,
    merchant=rf.Category,
    currency=rf.Enum(values=("USD", "EUR", "GBP")),
    disputed=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

One labeled payment:

```yaml
amount: 84.50
merchant: North Market
currency: USD
disputed: false
```

Every declared label is available immediately. Use [Category](category.qmd)
when training data should introduce labels over time. Add `mask=True` to an
Enum to predict one of its declared labels.

## Input and options

`values` is a required, nonempty tuple of unique labels. Use one exact built-in
Python type throughout the tuple: `bool`, `int`, `float`, `str`, or `bytes`.
Mixed types, null labels, NaN, and infinity are rejected. For example,
`values=(1, 2, 3)` declares integer labels; floating-point inputs must not be
used in their place. Arrow widths may differ within the declared type family.

Null inputs are separate [value states](index.qmd#value-state),
not members of `values`. An input outside the declared set raises an error in
training, validation, test, and prediction, including when the field is hidden
by a mask. Use a [preprocessor](../guides/preprocessing.qmd) to normalize
application-specific spellings or map unmatched inputs to a fallback label
that you include in `values`.

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `values` | Required | Nonempty tuple of unique labels of one built-in type; tuple order defines their internal indices. |
| `p_unavailable` | `0.01` | Training probability of replacing known valued input content with unavailable content. Reconstruction targets remain unchanged. |
| `topk` | `[]` | Sorted, unique integer accuracy cutoffs greater than one; also controls prediction candidates. Each cutoff is capped by the declared label count. |
| `strip` | `False` | Trim surrounding whitespace from string labels, in `values` and in every input alike. |
| `cased` | `True` | `False` lowercases string labels, in `values` and in every input alike; declarations that collide after folding are rejected. |

See [shared leaf options](index.qmd#shared-leaf-options)
for reconstruction, masking, and embedding configuration. Since `values` is
required, construct each field with `rf.Enum(values=(...))`.

## Fixed vocabulary and learning

Declaration order fixes the embedding and decoder rows. Training updates their
weights and records label counts without adding or reordering labels. All
declared labels participate in reconstruction and prediction from the start,
including labels that have not appeared in training.

```python
labels = rf.Enum.vocabulary(model, rf.Address("currency"))
counts = rf.Enum.counts(model, rf.Address("currency"))
```

`vocabulary` returns the declared tuple. It also accepts a preprocessor's
`encoding_context` in place of `model`. `counts` returns pristine valued
training exposures per declared label, including zero for unseen labels and
excluding nulls and padding. Repeated epochs count again; counts synchronize
across DDP ranks at epoch end. Evaluation and prediction do not update them.

Checkpoints preserve the declaration, learned weights, and counts. When an
existing model is rebuilt by a [schema mutation](../guides/schema-mutation.qmd),
an unchanged declaration preserves this field's learned state. Constructing a
new model starts fresh; load a checkpoint to restore training. Changing
`values` with `model.update(...)`, including changing their order, resets that
field's embedding, decoder, and counts.

Reconstruction uses unweighted state and categorical cross entropy. It shares
the [Category metrics](category.qmd#vocabulary-and-learning), with every valid
valued target inside the declared vocabulary.

## Prediction

`content` contains `value`, `probability`, and `topk`. Probabilities are
normalized over all declared labels. The candidate list has up to `max(topk)`
entries, capped by the declared label count, and is empty when no cutoffs are
configured. Labels are written as Arrow `large_string`, including when input
labels are numeric or Boolean.

A declared label may receive a prediction before it has training examples;
membership in the schema does not establish prediction quality. With only one
declared label, its conditional probability is one. Read content probabilities
alongside `state` and `inferred` in the
[prediction envelope](../reference/prediction-output.qmd).

The [fixed-class evidence](../evidence/enum/fixed-class-learning.html) compares
informative and shuffled context. The
[withheld-class evidence](../evidence/enum/declared-without-examples.html) follows a
declared class before and after it receives training examples.
The [held-out instruction evidence](../evidence/composition/held-out-requests.html)
tests whether familiar group and operation labels compose in combinations
excluded from training.
